newsitem.title: UK: NWE heating oil premiums revive, Russians ease.
newsitem.headline: NWE heating oil premiums revive, Russians ease.

text.p: NWE gas oil cargo activity perked up slightly on Wednesday despite a standoff over the November IPE delivery, with German demand boosting heating oil premiums and lack of buyers lowering those for Russians, traders said.

On the barge market premiums were stable but volumes were were muted by the standoff over the record high delivery that has cut availability of prompt vessels in ARA. The dispute had also curbed cargo trade, keeping wary traders out of the market.
Benchmark Dec IPE futures finished 75 cents lower at $216.25 per tonne, with Iraq's likely re-entry to the oil market outweighing a range of positive fundamentals.
Low sulphur diesel cargo traded at Dec IPE +17 into France, $3 firmer, and was talked at +$18.50/19 into Rostock. A heating oil cargo traded at +$5.75 into Bremen for early December
A U.S.-bound cargo of Russian that had passed the deviation point was traded back into Europe at Dec +0.50 basis Rotterdam, equivalent to around $1.50 lower, after the U.S. arb closed.
Heating oil barges traded at Dec IPE +$2 for early December and a low sulphur diesel traded at +$12.25, both fob Flushing.
An eastern arb appeared opening slowly as Singapore gas oil gains on buying interest from China.
